With respect to use of Condition Variable (CV), note that in addition to the CV, the wait() call takes a mutex lock as its second argument. State the dynamics of wait( ) call and explain the reason behind involving mutex lock in this design. Also briefly state the need for using a while() loop for the predicate check in the calling of the wait() operation.
questions.answer:
The wait() on CV, puts the caller to sleep + releases the lock (atomically), otherwise how could another thread acquire the lock and change the state and/or signal it to wake up? Also if putting to sleep + releases the lock both is not done atomically then also there is a race condition so that is also taken care by this call. Before returning after being woken up, wait() re-acquires the lock, thus ensuring that anytime the waiting thread is running between the lock acquired at the beginning of the wait sequence and the lock release at the end, it holds the lock. This design of wait() call thus is very convenient for application use so that programmer need not worry about concurrency issues coming up.
When a condition variable is signaled to wake up a thread, it is removed from the wait queue but before that thread reacquires the mutex, another thread may be given CPU time (and potentially the mutex). As a result, the shared state may be updated before the waking up thread reacquires the mutex. Therefore, the thread must do another check when it actually acquires the mutex to ensure the condition it needs to proceed is still true.

questions.text: Consider an application that has K + 1 threads running on a Linux‑like OS (K > 1). The first K threads of an application execute a certain task T1, and the remaining one thread executes task T2. The application logic requires that task T1 is executed N > 1 times, followed by task T2 to be executed once, and this cycle of N executions of T1 followed by one execution of T2 continue indefinitely. All K threads should be able to participate in the N executions of task T1, even though it is not required to ensure perfect fairness amongst the threads. Show a correct implementation of the functions of task T1 and task T2 using only locks and condition variables as synchronization primitives.
